questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The destination was of particular importance, along with the availability of courses that touched on subjects covered in the Social Data Science program.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was quite hard to find them via online ressources, but when writing directly to representatives of the university, I usually recieved answers somewhat quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were intro meetings for erasmus students as well as for the master programs.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I it is located just by a metro station.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That Paris metro are not always entirely reliable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was only officically registered for courses close to a month into the semester, which was odd and somewhat disapointing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I filled out the desired courses in my learning agreement prior to the begininning of the semester and later confirmed them with a secretary

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The secretaries were very helpful, but the online ressources are very confusing, too segmented, and not entirely synchronized.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the courses I wished for. One courses was no longer offered. I was informed of this after filling out the original learning agreement.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Confirm whether the courses that are advertised are actually still active.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My courses included way more concrete prequisites that could not be read directly from the course descriptions, this made them quite challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were very few student presentations, and more home assignments. I did not particulaty dislike this. I will hovewer say that the general workload is significantly larger than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
VISION: Advanced Methods for Computer Vision,
PRAT: Image Seminar and Projects,
RDFIA: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning for Image Understanding,
BIMA: Fundamentals of Image Processing,
TADI: Advanced Methods for Image Analysis.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: PRAT: Image Seminar and Projects. This course allows students to go in depth with a particular assigned topic within computer vision. This learning outcome is huge, as students are expected to competently organize their own work.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The Cité Internationale were I was afforded housing through the host instituion charges extra fees for guests.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was not suprised by prices as a whole.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Music, sports and other social activites were offered. I did not see to many debate-focused activities which would have been nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I made more use of the services offered Cité internationale, where I lived during my stay, wherefore I cannot judge the activites offered by the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Many musuems are free for persons under the age of 26, which is a very nice thing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found all things digital (e.g. certain services offered by the university, banks and the like) to be way more challenging to find and use than it is the case in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I thouroughly enjoyed the amount of very affordable restaurants and cafés. Additionally, museums are much more affordable.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find all additional information on the courses you wish to take, whether from past participants or via asking the representatives from the university.
2. Get to know the metro lines.
3. Visit museum and look for student discounts.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: While not located in the center, the Cité Internationale has good facilites and provides a good place to study and socialize.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: After having completed the stay, I now feel like I can face most academical challenges with a level head.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: By far the greatest challenge was finding in depth information about the courses, prior to being granted access to the platforms used by the host university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
